newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean oil products weak, except naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean oil products weak, except naphtha.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all weaker on Monday, except naphtha which was steady, traders said.
Gasoline prices fell slightly and traders said the Med did not appear to be as strong as northwest Europe.
Unleaded premium cargoes fell about $2 to $233/$234 cif. "It is not as strong as northwest Europe...In the Med, all the needs are covered," a trader said.
He said three to four cargoes of premium leaded were on offer out of Italy, with at least one cargo each from southern France and Greece.
Naphtha was unchanged at $216/$218 cif for cargoes. High freight rates, traders said, have hampered sending cargoes to northwest Europe and quieted trade.
Gas oil slipped by about $3.00 per tonne as excess U.S. supply, especially diesel, continued to pour into Europe where demand is still low.

But Mediterranean markets held up better than the north, partly because traders were hoping to cover a substantial proportion of India's December tender with cargoes from Italy, Lavera and Constanza -- big ports for large ships.

Fuel oil was softer. A Turkish tender for 55-60,000 tonnes of low sulphur and 25-50,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel was won by a trader, but no price levels were initially available. Traders said the tender had given little support to prices.

Bunker grade fuel was still hard to come by, but prices were nevertheless easier with $110 cif Med a level talked, off nearly $3 from Friday, although nothing was heard concluded. Low sulphur cracked fuel was heard offered as low as $128 cif Italy on good supplies. The last done trade, on Wedensday Oct 30 was done at $130.
